newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in sleepy trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in sleepy trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in late Monday trade, dealers said.
One major local bank dealer said operators were staying on the sidelines on lack of motivation.
"There is not much downside for dollars at present. I also can't see any reason for an upturn," the dealer said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,322.1/22.60 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,322.50/23.50.
He said operators tended to be sidelined this week ahead of a public holiday in the United States next Monday.
"If you buy dollars now, it will be due on Wednesday. But on that day sentiment would probably be bearish ahead of the U.S. holiday due to longer spot dates," the dealer said.
"This seems to explain why the market is so quiet at present," he said, adding that there was also no reason to sell dollars because of the central bank's floor rate.
"The risk-ratio has increased. The potential gain is not really attractive for us to sell dollars now," the dealer said.
Short-dated swap rates remained expensive, keeping roll-over costs high and discouraging long dollar speculation, one said.
Both overnight and tom/next swaps closed at 0.60/0.65.
Dealers said longer-term swap rates were stable.
One-month swap was last at 19.00/19.50, two at 33.50/35.00, three at 51.25/52.00 and six at 100.5/101.5 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,318/2,510 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,318/2,366 on Monday.
